{\scriptsize\textit{Notes:} Single-factor $\hat\beta_{MKT}$ ($\alpha$ fixed at zero). North America, vintages up to 2010 (FW baseline: within-vintage median fund-size imputation; sensitivity in Table~\ref{tab:fw_imputation_sensitivity}): Buyout 25 vintages; VC 27, of which the 23 with at least two funds enter $U_{v,H}$. $U_{v,H}$: the cross-fund pair-product criterion with equal vintage weights ($q_v=1$); under Theorem~T7 (conditional independence of funds given the factor path, eligibility $n_v\ge2$, fund sizes, and vintage origin, zero sign-aligned conditional mean pricing error, no shared vintage effects $c_v=0$, and unique identification), it targets $\theta_0$ at every horizon, $H=0$ included. L2: per-commitment squared loss on vintage portfolios (under FW, matching the inverse-FoF-size dollar-portfolio normalization of \citealp[p.~533]{DLP12} at $H=0$, whereas EW averages per-dollar fund NPVs equally; unnormalized dollar sums scale each vintage squared error by $S_v^2$), whose target is tilted by within-vintage fund noise and moves with $H$ (matched-vintage 23-vintage VC L2 reported in Table~\ref{tab:iv_comparison}). SE: Bartlett sandwich over vintage years, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$. Markers on $U_{v,H}$: two-sided fixed-$b$ $p$-values of a test of $\beta=0$, $^{*}$\,$p<0.05$, $^{**}$\,$p<0.01$, $^{***}$\,$p<0.001$; column $p_1$ gives the two-sided fixed-$b$ $p$-value of $\beta=1$ (under shared shocks T8, per-vintage score centering can fail at $H>0$, Remark~\ref{rem:per_vintage_centering}). FW single-factor markers are qualified by mild finite-sample over-rejection (8.1\% Buyout / 8.5\% VC at $H=0$ in Design~B, Table~\ref{tab:mc_hardening}). $^{\dagger}$: estimate on a bound of the admissible domain ($\beta\in[-1,4]$, $\alpha\in[-2\%,2\%]$ per month, gross benchmark return at least 0.08), no SE. The headline estimate is $U_{v,H}$ at $H=0$: in our data-shaped core Monte Carlo, $H=0$ minimizes $U_{v,H}$ RMSE for single-factor $\beta$ and $(\alpha,\beta)$ (whereas in two-factor models, Table~\ref{tab:mc_two_factor}, $H=15$ yr lowers $U_{v,H}$'s second-loading RMSE for ME, IA, and ROE while market-beta RMSE rises in ROE). All horizons: Table~\ref{tab:u_l2_beta_all}.}
